holidays.name: Waffle Day (Våffeldagen)
holidays.description: A Swedish celebration where people gather to eat waffles topped with jam, whipped cream, or berries. It is a cozy excuse to fire up the waffle iron and indulge in a crispy, golden treat.
holidays.origin: The day falls on Lady Day (the Feast of the Annunciation), which in Swedish is 'Vårfrudagen.' Over time the name was mispronounced as 'Våffeldagen,' meaning Waffle Day, and the tradition of eating waffles stuck.
holidays.funFact: The holiday exists because of a linguistic mix-up: 'Vårfrudagen' (Our Lady's Day) sounded so much like 'Våffeldagen' that Swedes started eating waffles to mark it.

holidays.name: International Waffle Day
holidays.description: The global cousin of Sweden's Waffle Day, celebrated by waffle lovers everywhere with syrup, fruit, fried chicken, ice cream, or whatever else fits in the grid pockets.
holidays.origin: It spread from the Swedish tradition of Våffeldagen and was embraced by food fans and restaurants worldwide as a reason to serve up waffle specials.
holidays.funFact: The waffle iron was patented in the US in 1869 by Cornelius Swarthout, and the grid pattern is designed to hold maximum syrup.

holidays.name: Tolkien Reading Day
holidays.description: Fans of Middle-earth around the world read passages from J.R.R. Tolkien's works, host themed gatherings, and quote hobbits, elves, and wizards with great enthusiasm.
holidays.origin: Created in 2003 by the Tolkien Society, the date marks the fall of the Dark Lord Sauron in The Lord of the Rings, which happens on March 25 in the story's calendar.
holidays.funFact: Each year the Tolkien Society picks a different theme for the day, and the date was chosen for the destruction of the One Ring in the story rather than for any real-world event.

holidays.name: Pecan Day
holidays.description: A nutty celebration of the buttery pecan, perfect for baking pies, pralines, and snacking by the handful.
holidays.origin: Pecan Day is traditionally tied to the nut's agricultural heritage in the American South, where growers and bakers celebrate the native North American nut.
holidays.funFact: The pecan is the only major tree nut native to North America, and its name comes from an Algonquian word meaning 'nut requiring a stone to crack.'

holidays.name: International Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Slavery and the Transatlantic Slave Trade
holidays.description: A solemn observance honoring those who suffered and died under the brutality of the slave trade, and promoting education about its legacy and the dangers of racism.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007 to remember the victims and raise awareness of racism and prejudice today.
holidays.funFact: The UN marks it with events and educational programs, and the 2007 resolution coincided with the 200th anniversary of Britain's Slave Trade Act of 1807.
